seo.title: Generative Engine Optimization Agency: What They Do
seo.meta_description: What a generative engine optimization agency actually does, what a good engagement includes, and how to tell if your brand needs one yet.

h1: Generative Engine Optimization Agency: What It Does and When You Need One
answer: A generative engine optimization agency gets your brand found, trusted and cited by AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews. It audits how those engines describe you today, fixes what blocks them, restructures key pages into quotable answers, and builds the outside signals that make AI recommend you.
key_takeaways: A GEO agency works on being cited inside AI answers, not only on ranking a link.
Good engagements start with an audit of what each AI engine says about you today.
Most of the work is technical access, page structure, quotable content and brand authority.
GEO builds on SEO: AI answers lean heavily on pages search engines can already crawl and trust.
Judge an agency on measurement and transparency, not on promises about placement.

sections.heading: What a generative engine optimization agency actually does
sections.body_html:
Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the practice of making a brand easy for AI systems to find, understand, trust and quote. A generative engine optimization agency does that work for you across the engines your buyers use: ChatGPT, Google Gemini and AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude and Microsoft Copilot.

The goal is different from classic SEO. A search result page shows ten links and lets the buyer choose. An AI answer usually names a handful of brands, explains why, and links to a few sources. If you are not one of those names, you are invisible for that question, even if you rank on page one.

So a GEO agency asks a specific question for every topic that matters to your business: when a buyer asks an AI assistant about this, does it mention us, describe us correctly, and link to us? Then it works on the gaps.

sections.heading: The core services in a GEO engagement
sections.body_html:
Engagements vary, but a complete generative engine optimization agency covers six areas:

  1. AI visibility audit. Running your buyers' real questions through each engine and recording who gets mentioned, how you are described, and which sources are cited.
  2. Technical access. Making sure AI crawlers such as OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot can reach your pages, that pages are indexed, and that nothing important is hidden behind scripts or logins.
  3. Machine-readable structure. Organization, Service, Article and FAQ schema, a clean sitemap and an llms.txt file that maps your most useful pages.
  4. GEO content structuring. Rewriting key pages at passage level: direct answers at the top, question-style headings, comparison tables and specific, sourced facts.
  5. Entity and authority building. Consistent brand descriptions across your site, profiles, directories and earned mentions, so engines can confidently connect your name to your specialty.
  6. Citation tracking. Re-testing the same questions over time and reporting mentions, citations and AI-referred visits and leads.

sections.heading: How a GEO agency differs from an SEO agency
sections.body_html:
There is real overlap. Google states that the same fundamentals apply to its AI features as to Search: helpful, reliable content that can be crawled and indexed. Many AI answers cite pages that already rank well. That is why a serious GEO agency keeps SEO running in parallel rather than replacing it.

Traditional SEO agencyGenerative engine optimization agency
Main goalRank pages in search resultsBe named and cited inside AI answers
Unit of workPages and keywordsPassages, entities and questions
Key signalsLinks, relevance, technical healthClear answers, sourced facts, brand mentions, crawl access for AI bots
ReportingRankings, clicks, impressionsMentions and citations per engine, AI referral traffic, leads

The difference is emphasis. An SEO agency asks how to rank a page. A GEO agency asks whether an AI system would choose your page, or your brand, as the answer.

sections.heading: Signs your business is ready for a GEO agency
sections.body_html:
GEO pays off fastest when buyers research before they contact anyone. You are a good fit if:

  • Your buyers compare providers, read reviews and ask for recommendations before they buy.
  • You sell a service, software or a considered purchase rather than an impulse product.
  • Competitors are already being named when you test questions in ChatGPT or Perplexity.
  • You have a clear specialty an AI engine could describe in one sentence.
  • Your website already works: it loads, it is indexed, and it has a way to contact you.

When to wait

If your site has almost no indexed pages, no clear offer, or no contact path, fix those basics first. GEO amplifies what is already there. It does not replace a working website or a product people want.

sections.heading: What a good first 90 days looks like
sections.body_html:
A credible generative engine optimization agency should be able to show you a plan like this before you sign:

  • Weeks 1–2: diagnose. A baseline of how each engine answers your top 30–50 buyer questions, plus a technical audit of crawl access, indexing and structured data.
  • Weeks 2–4: fix. Unblock AI crawlers, repair indexing problems, add schema and llms.txt, and set up tracking for AI referrers and form submissions.
  • Weeks 4–8: structure and content. Rebuild the pages that matter most and publish new pages that answer high-intent questions directly.
  • Weeks 8–12: authority and measurement. Start earning mentions in places engines trust, re-run the baseline questions, and report what moved.

Expect early citations on specific, long-tail questions first. Broad, competitive questions take longer, and nobody controls what an AI model says on a given day.

sections.heading: How to measure what a GEO agency delivers
sections.body_html:
Vague reports are the biggest risk with any new discipline. Ask for numbers you can check yourself:

  • Mentions and citations: for a fixed list of buyer questions, how often each engine names you or links to you, month over month.
  • AI referral traffic: visits from chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com and claude.ai, grouped as their own channel in Google Analytics.
  • Leads by source: form submissions tied to the page and the engine that sent the visitor.
  • Search health: indexed pages, impressions and clicks from Google Search Console.

If an agency cannot explain how it will measure progress, or promises a fixed position inside ChatGPT, treat that as a warning sign.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before you hire
sections.body_html:
1. Can you show me what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity say about my brand today?
  2. Which of my pages would you change first, and why?
  3. How do you handle crawl access for AI bots, and which ones do you allow?
  4. What does your monthly report contain, and can I see an example?
  5. How do you keep traditional SEO healthy while doing GEO?
  6. What will you need from my team each month?

A strong agency answers these with specifics about your site, not with a generic deck.

faqs.q: What does a generative engine optimization agency do?
faqs.a: It improves how AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews find, describe and cite your brand. The work covers an AI visibility audit, technical crawl access, schema and llms.txt, rewriting key pages into quotable answers, building brand authority, and tracking citations and AI-referred leads.

faqs.q: Is a GEO agency different from an SEO agency?
faqs.a: Yes, in emphasis. SEO focuses on ranking pages in search results, while GEO focuses on being named and cited inside AI answers. The two overlap heavily, so a good GEO agency keeps SEO running in parallel.

faqs.q: How long does it take to see results from a GEO agency?
faqs.a: Most brands see technical fixes and first citations on specific questions within the first two to three months. Competitive, broad questions take longer, and results depend on how quickly pages are indexed and how strong your existing authority is.

faqs.q: Can a GEO agency guarantee my brand appears in ChatGPT?
faqs.a: No. Nobody controls what an AI model says, and answers change over time. A good agency improves the odds by making your brand the clearest, best-supported option to cite, and shows the change with measurement.

faqs.q: What should a GEO agency report every month?
faqs.a: Mentions and citations for a fixed set of buyer questions in each engine, visits from AI referrers, leads by source page, and search health from Google Search Console. You should be able to verify each number yourself.

faqs.q: Do small businesses need a generative engine optimization agency?
faqs.a: Small specialists often benefit most, because AI engines can describe a clear niche more easily than a broad generalist. Start with the questions your best customers ask before they buy and check whether AI assistants mention you for them.
